name: The Heart
description: A muscular organ that pumps blood through the vessels of the circulatory system, delivering oxygen and nutrients throughout the body.

keyFacts.label: Size
keyFacts.value: About the size of a fist

medicalImportance: Central motor of systemic perfusion. Coronary occlusion triggers acute myocardial infarction; valve failure causes congestive edema.
didYouKnow: The heart generates its own electrical impulses via the SA node and can beat outside the body if supplied with oxygen.

microscopicView.title: Cardiac myocytes & discs
microscopicView.subtitle: Myocardial striations
microscopicView.description: Intercalated discs, branching striations, desmosomes, and gap junctions synchronizing electrical excitation.

compareData.subtitle: Heart vs. lungs
compareData.description: Systemic vascular high pressure versus pulmonary capillary low-resistance alveolar exchange.

quote.text: Learning is an act of curiosity.

parts.name: Left Ventricle
parts.description: The primary systemic pumping chamber forming the apex and diaphragmatic surface of the heart. Possesses a circular cross-section with myocardium 3× thicker (8-12 mm) than the right ventricle to overcome systemic vascular resistance (SVR).
parts.function: Generates systemic systolic pressure (typically 120 mmHg) to eject stroke volume (approx. 70 mL) through the aortic valve into the systemic arterial circulation.
connections: Receives oxygenated inflow from Left Atrium via Bicuspid (Mitral) Valve
Ejects outflow through Aortic Semilunar Valve into Ascending Aorta
Bound medially by the muscular Interventricular Septum
Anchored by Anterior and Posterior Papillary Muscles with Chordae Tendineae
parts.clinicalNote: Hypertrophy occurs in chronic systemic hypertension and aortic stenosis. Critical auscultation point: 5th intercostal space, left midclavicular line (point of maximal impulse / PMI). Failure leads to acute pulmonary edema, orthopnea, and crackles.
keyFeatures: Normal ejection fraction: 55% - 70%
Myocardial wall thickness: 8 - 12 mm
Peak systolic pressure generation: 100 - 140 mmHg
Susceptible to anterior myocardial infarction via LAD occlusion
parts.histology: Thick branched cardiac myocytes with single central nuclei, dense intercalated discs with gap junctions, and extensive transverse T-tubule networks.

parts.name: Aortic Arch & Root
parts.description: The principal elastic arterial conduit arising from the base of the left ventricle at the level of the 3rd left costal cartilage, curving posterosuperiorly over the pulmonary root and left principal bronchus before continuing as the descending thoracic aorta at T4.
parts.function: Functions as a high-capacitance Windkessel elastic reservoir, expanding during left ventricular systole to dampen pulse pressure and recoiling during diastole to maintain continuous peripheral and coronary perfusion.
connections: Arises from Left Ventricular outflow tract at Aortic Valve orifice
Gives off Left and Right Coronary Arteries from Sinuses of Valsalva
Branches superiorly: Brachiocephalic trunk, Left common carotid, Left subclavian artery
Connected to left pulmonary artery via Ligamentum Arteriosum
parts.clinicalNote: Type A aortic dissection (Stanford) is a surgical emergency characterized by tearing chest pain radiating to the interscapular back. Baroreceptors in the aortic arch wall (innervated by CN X) modulate blood pressure homeostasis.
keyFeatures: Average luminal diameter: 25 - 30 mm at root
Windkessel effect drives 65% of coronary diastolic perfusion
Houses high-pressure baroreceptors tuned to mean arterial pressure (MAP)
Vulnerable to deceleration shearing injury at aortic isthmus
parts.histology: Tunica media comprises 40-70 concentric fenestrated elastic laminae interspersed with vascular smooth muscle cells and type III collagen fibrils.

parts.name: Pulmonary Trunk & Arteries
parts.description: A thick, short (approx. 5 cm) major vascular conduit emerging anterior to the ascending aorta from the infundibulum (conus arteriosus) of the right ventricle, ascending posterolaterally to bifurcate beneath the aortic arch at the level of T5 into right and left pulmonary arteries.
parts.function: Carries total deoxygenated venous return from the right ventricle into the low-resistance, high-capacitance pulmonary microvascular capillary bed for carbon dioxide elimination and blood oxygenation.
connections: Originates at Pulmonary Orifice guarded by Pulmonary Semilunar Valve (anterior, right, left cusps)
Ascends anterior then lateral to the Ascending Aorta within fibrous pericardium
Bifurcates into Right Pulmonary Artery (courses posterior to ascending aorta/SVC) and Left Pulmonary Artery (anterior to descending aorta)
Anchored to aortic concavity by Ligamentum Arteriosum
parts.clinicalNote: Saddle pulmonary embolism lodges at this bifurcation, producing acute right heart strain (cor pulmonale), obstructive shock, jugular venous distention, and sudden arrest. Mean normal pulmonary arterial pressure is 10-20 mmHg; >25 mmHg indicates pulmonary hypertension.
keyFeatures: Normal pulmonary arterial systolic/diastolic pressure: 15-25 / 8-15 mmHg
Low vascular resistance: ~1/10th of systemic vascular resistance
Carries oxygen-depleted blood (SaO2 ~70-75%) despite being an artery
Auscultation site: 2nd intercostal space, left sternal border
parts.histology: Elastic artery with thinner media than aorta; rich in compliant elastin fibers allowing accommodation of right ventricular cardiac output at lower hydrostatic pressures.

parts.name: Right Atrium
parts.description: Forms the right border of the heart. Characterized internally by a smooth posterior wall (sinus venarum) derived from the embryonic sinus venosus and a ridged anterior muscular wall featuring parallel pectinate muscles separated by the crista terminalis.
parts.function: Receives deoxygenated systemic venous return from the SVC, IVC, and cardiac venous return from the coronary sinus, acting as a passive reservoir and active booster pump during atrial systole into the right ventricle.
connections: Receives Superior Vena Cava (valveless, upper body return) at upper posterior border
Receives Inferior Vena Cava (guarded by Eustachian valve remnant) at lower posterior wall
Receives Coronary Sinus (Thebesian valve) between IVC orifice and AV orifice
Discharges through Tricuspid (Right AV) Valve into Right Ventricle
Interatrial septum presents Fossa Ovalis (limbus fossae ovalis) from closed foramen ovale
parts.clinicalNote: Houses the Sinoatrial (SA) node near the junction of SVC and crista terminalis, and the AV node within the Triangle of Koch. Central venous pressure (CVP) monitored here (normal: 2-6 mmHg). Atrial fibrillation triggers mural thrombi in the right atrial appendage.
keyFeatures: Normal central venous pressure (CVP): 2 - 8 mmHg
Hosts SA nodal primary pacemaker cells firing 60-100 bpm
Secretes Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) in response to atrial stretch/hypervolemia
Pectinate muscle architecture provides muscular contractility without excessive mass
parts.histology: Endocardium lined with simple squamous endothelial cells; thin myocardium containing specialized P-cells (pacemaker) in the SA node.

parts.name: Cardiac Apex
parts.description: The inferolateral blunt conical tip of the heart formed entirely by the inferolateral muscular wall of the left ventricle. Directed downwards, forwards, and to the left, resting upon the central tendon of the diaphragm.
parts.function: Acts as the terminal focal vector of ventricular electrical depolarization (via Purkinje network) and the fulcrum of helical myocardial wringing torsion that maximizes ejection fraction efficiency.
connections: Continuous superiorly with the free lateral and anterior walls of Left Ventricle
Traversed by terminal anastomosis of Left Anterior Descending (LAD) and Posterior Descending (PDA) arteries
Overlayed anteriorly by Left Lung cardiac notch and thin visceral pericardium
Corresponds surface-anatomically to the 5th left intercostal space, 7-9 cm from midsternal line
parts.clinicalNote: Point of maximal impulse (PMI) palpated here during cardiac exam. Lateral or inferior displacement beyond the midclavicular line signifies left ventricular cardiomegaly or volume overload. Apical ballooning syndrome (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy) selectively stuns this region.
keyFeatures: Site of apical pulse auscultation and stethoscope bell placement for S3/S4 gallops
Undergoes 10-15 degrees of wringing torsion during systole
Focal site for pericardiocentesis subxiphoid approach targeting apical recess
Dual blood supply via apical collateral network between LAD and PDA
parts.histology: Spiraling epicardial and endocardial muscular bundles forming the vortex cordis; covered by visceral serous pericardium with subepicardial adipose.

quizBank.prompt: Which chamber ejects blood into the systemic aorta?
quizBank.rationale: The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium to overcome systemic arterial resistance.
